steps.description: dp[i][x] will hold the fewest coins that make amount x using only the first i denominations of [1, 2, 5]. Because a coin may be reused, taking denomination i again will look back along ROW i itself, not up to row i-1 the way a 0/1-item table would.
Zero coins are needed to make amount 0, no matter which denominations are available yet — column x=0 is 0 all the way down.
With no denominations available yet, no positive amount is reachable: row "0 coins" is infinity everywhere except x=0.

Cell (1,1): skip coin 1 and carry down dp[0][1] = ∞ from the row above, or take ONE MORE coin 1 by reading dp[1][0] = 0 from THIS SAME ROW (a coin may be reused) and adding 1 = 1. Using one more coin 1 wins: 1.

Cell (1,2): skip coin 1 and carry down dp[0][2] = ∞ from the row above, or take ONE MORE coin 1 by reading dp[1][1] = 1 from THIS SAME ROW (a coin may be reused) and adding 1 = 2. Using one more coin 1 wins: 2.

Cell (1,3): skip coin 1 and carry down dp[0][3] = ∞ from the row above, or take ONE MORE coin 1 by reading dp[1][2] = 2 from THIS SAME ROW (a coin may be reused) and adding 1 = 3. Using one more coin 1 wins: 3.
